observation.visible_scene: A close-up, shallow-focus shot of a heaped pile of glossy roasted coffee beans filling the lower two-thirds of the frame, set against a warm, out-of-focus amber/golden background. Faint wisps of pale steam or smoke hover just above the bean surface. The lighting is soft and consistently warm throughout.
visible_changes: The image content drifts steadily to the left over the excerpt: a bright orange-toned bean at the lower left (prominent early) slides out of frame, while previously unseen beans enter on the right edge, indicating a slow lateral camera pan/tracking movement to the right across the pile.
The relative arrangement of the beans to one another stays fixed, so the apparent translation is camera motion, not the beans moving.
Thin steam/smoke plumes above the beans shift and re-form slightly (e.g., a wisp near the left-center early on is replaced by wisps elsewhere later), consistent with rising, drifting vapor.
The blurred background and overall warm color balance remain essentially constant.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the camera motion continues, reverses, or stops beyond these frames.
The source or cause of the steam (heat, smoke, or effect), and what lies outside the cropped field of view.
Any action before t=0 or after t≈2.67s.
uncertain_details: Whether the lateral motion is a pure pan (rotation) or a dolly/truck (translation) — background blur gives little parallax evidence to distinguish them.
Whether the faint vapor is steam from hot beans or smoke; its low contrast makes exact shape and direction of drift hard to track.
Minor bean-level shifts (e.g., settling) cannot be separated from camera motion at this resolution.

Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
